title: Lake
Katherine
thesis: Solo to an 11,700-foot lake under Santa Fe Baldy, from a paved trailhead forty minutes above Santa Fe. Nonstop in, cheapest car on the lot, no rough road. Josh — August 25 to 28, 2026.

profile.note: Trailhead, Puerto Nambe and Lake Katherine elevations are USGS 10-metre DEM values at surveyed coordinates, cross-checked against published figures. The drawn line hides a real dip: the trail descends into the Rio Nambe below mile 2 before climbing again.

why: This is the cheapest, lowest-friction alpine trip available from Austin. One nonstop to Albuquerque, the cheapest class of rental car, and NM-475 is paved the whole way to a trailhead at 10,272 feet — no forest road, no clearance question, no gate to open. Fifteen miles of walking gets a lake at 11,737 feet with Santa Fe Baldy, a 12,631-foot walk-up, directly above camp.

It also suits going alone. The Winsor Trail is the busiest trail in the Sangre de Cristos — a mountain-bike corridor for its first miles and a day-hiker highway to Nambe Lake — which means company, a beaten track, and a short bail-out the entire way. The trade is honest: Lake Katherine is a popular camp and you will not have it to yourself. On a solo trip that is a feature, not a cost.

days.title: Fly in, walk to the pass
log: Land Albuquerque, collect the car — cheapest class on the lot
I-25 north to Santa Fe. Groceries and a fuel canister on the way through
NM-475 up through Hyde Park to the ski basin, 15 winding miles
Winsor trailhead, 10,272 ft. Upper or lower lot, boots on
Camp 1 near Puerto Nambe, 11,104 ft — meadow at the trail junction, 200 ft off water
notes: 4.6 miles: a steep half mile to start, then the trail drops through aspen into the Rio Nambe and climbs to the pass. Short on purpose — it's the acclimatization day from 500 feet. Water at the Nambe crossing and at La Vega below the pass. Mind the cattle at La Vega.

days.title: The lake, and the peak if the sky allows
notes: 2.8 miles and 630 feet from Puerto Nambe to Lake Katherine: left at the pass, then tight switchbacks under the ridge into denser forest. Short enough to be at the lake by mid-morning with the whole day left.

Santa Fe Baldy, 12,631 feet, is the reason to be here early. Skyline Trail #251 climbs to a saddle roughly a thousand feet below the summit, and an unofficial ridge path finishes it — a walk-up in good conditions, nowhere to be in a storm. Solo rule: on the summit by noon under a clean sky, or not at all. Camp 2 at Lake Katherine, 200 feet back from the water.

days.title: Out, and into Santa Fe
notes: 7.4 miles back down, mostly gentle, with one genuine climb out of the Rio Nambe before the last mile to the lot. Four hours at a civilized pace.
Down NM-475 to a motel on Cerrillos Road, a shower, and the best plate in walking distance. The Plaza is ten minutes away if there's energy left for it.

days.title: Home
log: Santa Fe to the Albuquerque airport, about an hour. Drop the car
notes: There's also an 8:10 PM nonstop for the same fare if a slow morning in Santa Fe sounds better than an early one.

map.drive_note: I-25 north to Santa Fe, then St Francis Drive to Artist Road and NM-475 for 15 miles to the end of the pavement at Ski Santa Fe. No dirt, no clearance requirement — the cheapest car on the lot does this.
map.caveat: The diagram is the offline and print fallback — no network, survives a dead phone. The dashed line is straight-line spacing between surveyed waypoints, not the trail. It understates the walking badly: the trailhead sits four straight-line miles from the lake but seven and a half trail miles, because the route drops into the Rio Nambe and climbs back over a pass. Carry the paper sheet.

route.title: Winsor trailhead, Ski Santa Fe
route.body: End of NM-475, fifteen miles above town. Upper and lower lots, restrooms, and no wilderness permit needed anywhere in the Pecos. Trail #254 leaves from the left as you pull in. Elevation from the USGS 10-metre DEM at the Forest Service trailhead coordinate; the agency lists the trail topping out at 10,293 ft, which agrees.

route.title: The only steep half mile
route.body: A stiff climb to the wilderness boundary fence, then it flattens. At the boundary keep straight — the path breaking right climbs Raven's Ridge, a fine walk and the wrong one today.

route.title: Left at the Y
route.body: The trail has been descending through aspen into the Rio Nambe. At the signed Y, go left for Puerto Nambe and Lake Katherine. Right is the spur to Nambe Lake — the most popular day hike in the range, and a dead end for this trip. Water at the Nambe crossing just past the junction; the footbridge has needed repair in recent years.

route.title: La Vega, then the pass
route.body: Open meadow with water and, most summers, cattle. Above it the trail climbs steadily to Puerto Nambe. Last easy water before camp is here.

route.title: Puerto Nambe — Camp 1
route.body: A broad meadow pass where Skyline Trail #251 splits off. Good dispersed camping in the trees at the edges — 200 feet off water, 50 feet off the trail, per Pecos Wilderness rules. Storms rake this pass in the afternoon; it is not a place to be caught high and late.

photo.caption: Santa Fe Baldy (right) and Pecos Baldy across the Pecos high country

route.title: Left, and up the switchbacks
route.body: From the pass, left toward Lake Katherine; right runs to Spirit Lake, which is the sheltered alternative if the weather is ugly and has good established sites of its own. The Katherine line climbs about 630 feet in tight switchbacks under the ridge. The Forest Service numbers the final branch Lake Katherine Trail #242 and gives it 1.3 miles, so roughly half this segment is still on #254 and #251 — trust the signs over the arithmetic.

route.title: Lake Katherine — Camp 2
route.body: A cirque lake directly under the north face of Santa Fe Baldy. Camping and campfires are prohibited within 200 feet of the lake, and the Forest Service says plainly that Katherine is heavily impacted and asks people to camp elsewhere where they can — worth taking seriously, and worth arriving early enough to have the choice. Volunteer rangers do check and will move you.

route.title: Santa Fe Baldy, if the morning is clean
route.body: Back to the Skyline saddle and up the ridge — a walk-up with no technical difficulty in good conditions, about a thousand feet from the saddle. Wholly exposed. Alone, this is a before-noon proposition with a hard turnaround, no exceptions.

route.title: The return
route.body: Reverse it: down the switchbacks, right at Puerto Nambe, past La Vega, across the Nambe, then the one real climb of the day back to the boundary fence and a final easy half mile down to the lot. Four hours or so, and the last stretch has cell signal well before the car.

rows.note: Southwest nonstop, Tue Aug 25 out / Fri Aug 28 back. Google Flights, checked 2026-07-28, rated typical pricing.

None required anywhere in the Pecos Wilderness.

hazard.title: Exposed ground, alone, in monsoon season
hazard.intro: This is an easy trail with one serious hazard: everything above Puerto Nambe is open, high, and directly in the path of the afternoon storms that build here most days in August. Solo removes the margin — nobody to go for help, nobody to argue you out of a bad call.
points: Puerto Nambe and the Baldy ridge by noon. The pass and the summit ridge are both fully exposed. Turn around alone, on schedule, with nobody watching.
Satellite messenger on your body, not in the pack, with a check-in someone at home is actually watching. They get the route, the camps, the plate, and a walk-out deadline before you leave.
Hang everything scented. Black bears, no grizzlies, no canister rule — a proper hang or Ursack, well away from the tent.
Respect the 200-foot rule at the lake. Rangers check Katherine, and a drought year makes the shoreline damage worse. Arrive early enough to have a legal site.
Altitude, fast. Austin to 11,100 feet in one afternoon. The short first day is the plan; drink ahead of thirst and treat a headache as information.
hazard.outro: The trail's popularity is the safety net here. Use it — camp near other people, and tell someone the plan.

weather.intro: Late August is the back half of the monsoon: clear mornings, storms building over the divide by early afternoon most days, gone by dark. 2026's monsoon came late but strong over a severe-drought base. These are station normals, not a forecast.
weather.source: Terrero co-op station normals (7,714 ft, WRCC, 1946–61 record) — the nearest mountain station, in the Pecos canyon over the divide. Lake figures lapse-rate derived, hence the ~; canyon-bottom lows overstate the spread, so plan for low 30s and possible frost. Checked 2026-07-28.

before.p: Stage II restrictions (no wood or charcoal fires; stoves only, in a cleared area) were ordered forest-wide June 26 through September 30, 2026 — though the order had dropped off the Santa Fe NF alerts page by July 28 with no rescission announced. Plan stove-only and check the alerts page the week of.
The Rio Nambe crossing, La Vega, and the lake are the reliable sources; the stretch between La Vega and the lake is dry. Filter everything, and top off at La Vega before the pass.
The trailhead is already at 10,272 feet — higher than most Colorado trailheads. Camp one at 11,104 is the acclimatization night, and the short first day exists for that reason alone.

NM-475 is paved, winding, and busy on weekends. The lots at the ski basin fill on August weekends; a Tuesday is fine. No forest road, no clearance question — this is the trip's whole logistical argument.
There is usually service at the ski basin and on the upper switchbacks, and none in the Nambe drainage or at the lake. Send the itinerary before you start walking.

No permit needed. Camping and campfires prohibited within 200 feet of any lake and within 50 feet of trails and streams. Lake Katherine is heavily used and the Forest Service asks people to spread out — Puerto Nambe and Spirit Lake both hold legal, quieter sites.

booking.title: Flight — $217, Aug 25 out, Aug 28 back
booking.body: Times were read live on July 28 and repeat daily, but Southwest reshuffles schedules — recheck when booking. The Monday–Thursday pair costs $237.

booking.title: The cheapest car they have
booking.body: About $231 for three days at Albuquerque. Nothing about this drive needs clearance, so take the smallest thing on the lot and put the difference toward the motel.

booking.title: One motel night in Santa Fe, Thursday
booking.body: Cerrillos Road, $84–130. Tourist-season Santa Fe does fill; don't leave it to the final days.

booking.title: Call the Española ranger district — (505) 753-7331
booking.body: This side of the wilderness is the Española district, not Pecos. Ask about fire restrictions and current trail conditions above Puerto Nambe.

lines: Trailhead: 35.7956, −105.8049 · Winsor Trailhead #254, end of NM-475, Ski Santa Fe
Española Ranger District, Santa Fe National Forest · (505) 753-7331
Recommended map: Outdoor Trail Maps, Santa Fe & Pecos Wilderness (2023) — or the USGS Aspen Basin quad
open_questions: Mileages come from local trail guides (2.4 mi to the Y, 2.2 more to Puerto Nambe, 2.8 more to Lake Katherine). The Forest Service gives Lake Katherine Trail #242 as only 1.3 miles, so the segment splits across three trail numbers — the total is consistent but the internal breakdown is not firmly sourced.

All elevations here are USGS 10-metre DEM values read at surveyed coordinates. They agree closely with published figures (lake 11,737 vs 11,742 cited; Baldy 12,631 vs 12,632), which is the cross-check, but no single trip report states the whole profile.

Straight-line to trail-mile ratio on this route runs about 1.85 — well outside the normal band. That is real, not an error: the trail drops into the Rio Nambe and crosses a pass. The diagram understates the walking.
Stage II fire restrictions were ordered through Sept 30 but had dropped off the forest's alert page by July 28 with no rescission found — status ambiguous, verify by phone.
Commons has no freely licensed photograph of Lake Katherine itself; the one photo here shows Santa Fe Baldy from a distance.
